summary: David A. Dilworth works in philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968), and held a post at Stony Brook University around 1970.

David A. Hall is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed his doctorate at UC Berkeley (1990) and studied under Shoshin Ichishima (1976). He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and department chair at Montgomery College (attested 2019).
David Azzopardi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman, held a fellowship at Rice University, and was Associate Professor at Santa Clara University (attested 2008–2017).

David Brown (1762–1812) was an active figure in religious studies and Indology. He studied under Joseph Milner and at Magdalene College, Cambridge, later serving as Provost of Fort William College in 1800 and founding the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society.

David Bubna-Litic earned a PhD from Western Sydney University (attested 2000). Active in Buddhist studies, he served as a Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney (attested 2000).

David Burton specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997) and served as Senior Lecturer in Theology and Religious Studies at Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).

David Dean Shulman is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from SOAS, University of London (1972–1976) under John Ralston Marr, and served as Professor of Indian Studies and Comparative Religion at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1988–2017).

David Drewes is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Virginia (2006) under Karen Christina Lang. He served as an instructor at Virginia, visiting lecturer at Indiana University (2006), and assistant professor at Manitoba (2009–2010).

David E. Cooper is a philosopher who studied at St Edmund Hall (~1960–1964). He served as a lecturer at the University of Oxford (1967), Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008), and Distinguished International Visiting Professor at Peking University (2022).

David E. Riggs, a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, earned his Ph.D. from UCLA. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and University of Hawaiʻi, later holding research posts at Nichibunken (attested 2006) and Oberlin College (attested 2010).

David Faure is a historian and sinologist who studied at the University of Hong Kong and earned a PhD from Princeton (~1970–1975). He taught at Indiana University, St Antony's College (1990–2006), and served as director at Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2006–2017).

David Fiordalis specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez (attested 2008) and became associate professor and chair of religious studies at Linfield University (attested 2017).

David Friedman (1903–1984) was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS and Professor at the University of London from circa 1950 to 1970.

David Germano is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1992). He served as Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia (attested 2000–2008).
David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Chicago (~1979–1988). He taught at the University of Virginia (1986, 1994–1996) and became Professor of Comparative Religion at UC Santa Barbara in 1996.

David J. Kalupahana (1936–2014) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at SOAS (1964–1966). He taught at the University of Peradeniya (~1959–1972) and chaired the Department of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi from 1972.

David Jones is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Hawaiʻi. Attested in 2007, he served as a professor of philosophy in the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt (1937–2006) was a historian who completed his doctorate at Cornell University (~1960–1966). He taught at SOAS (~1962–1968) and the University of Michigan (~1968–1969), and served as History Department Chair at Cornell (1969–2002).
